                      [32m'# Web Sockets\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp provides a fully integrated WebSocket experience by utilizing [Socket.IO](https://socket.io/) on the client and server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We handle making sure your URLs are correctly setup, CORS is enabled, and provide a useful `useSocket` and `useSocketListener` abstractions for use in React components.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To get started, you need to:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Define your WebSocket logic on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Enable WebSockets in your Wasp file, and connect it with your server logic.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Use WebSockets on the client, in React, via `useSocket` and `useSocketListener`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Optionally, type the WebSocket events and payloads for full-stack type safety.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's go through setting up WebSockets step by step, starting with enabling WebSockets in your Wasp file.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Turn On WebSockets in Your Wasp File\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We specify that we are using WebSockets by adding `webSocket` to our `app` and providing the required `fn`. You can optionally change the auto-connect behavior.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { webSocketFn } from "./src/webSocket" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  name: "myApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  webSocket: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    fn: webSocketFn,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    autoConnect: true, // optional, default: true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Defining the Events Handler\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's define the WebSockets server with all of the events and handler functions.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Full-stack type safety]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Check this out: we'll define the event types and payloads on the server, and they will be **automatically exposed on the client**. This helps you avoid mistakes when emitting events or handling them.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### `webSocketFn` Function {#websocketfn}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'On the server, you will get Socket.IO `io: Server` argument and `context` for your WebSocket function. The `context` object give you access to all of the entities from your Wasp app.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use this `io` object to register callbacks for all the regular [Socket.IO events](https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-api/). Also, if a user is logged in, you will have a `socket.data.user` on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is how we can define our `webSocketFn` function:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/webSocket.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { v4 as uuidv4 } from "uuid"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type WebSocketDefinition, type WaspSocketData } from "wasp/server/webSocket"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const webSocketFn: WebSocketFn = (io, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  io.on("connection", (socket) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    const username = socket.data.user?.getFirstProviderUserId() ?? "Unknown"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    console.log("a user connected: ", username)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    socket.on("chatMessage", async (msg) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      console.log("message: ", msg)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      io.emit("chatMessage", { id: uuidv4(), username, text: msg })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      // You can also use your entities here:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      // await context.entities.SomeEntity.create({ someField: msg })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Typing our WebSocket function with the events and payloads\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// allows us to get type safety on the client as well\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type WebSocketFn = WebSocketDefinition<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ClientToServerEvents,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ServerToClientEvents,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  InterServerEvents,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  SocketData\n'[39m +
                      [32m'>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface ServerToClientEvents {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  chatMessage: (msg: { id: string, username: string, text: string }) => void;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface ClientToServerEvents {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  chatMessage: (msg: string) => void;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface InterServerEvents {}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Data that is attached to the socket.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// NOTE: Wasp automatically injects the JWT into the connection,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// and if present/valid, the server adds a user to the socket.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface SocketData extends WaspSocketData {}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Using the WebSocket On The Client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Full-stack type safety]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All the hooks we use are typed with the events and payloads you defined on the server. VS Code will give you autocomplete for the events and payloads, and you will get type errors if you make a mistake.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### The `useSocket` Hook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Client access to WebSockets is provided by the `useSocket` hook. It returns:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `socket: Socket` for sending and receiving events.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `isConnected: boolean` for showing a display of the Socket.IO connection status.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  - Note: Wasp automatically connects and establishes a WebSocket connection from the client to the server by default, so you do not need to explicitly `socket.connect()` or `socket.disconnect()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  - If you set `autoConnect: false` in your Wasp file, then you should call these as needed.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All components using `useSocket` share the same underlying `socket`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### The `useSocketListener` Hook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Additionally, there is a `useSocketListener: (event, callback) => void` hook which is used for registering event handlers. It takes care of unregistering the handler on unmount.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp's **full-stack type safety** kicks in here: all the event types and payloads are automatically inferred from the server and are available on the client.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can additionally use the `ClientToServerPayload` and `ServerToClientPayload` helper types to get the payload type for a specific event.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/ChatPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import React, { useState } from "react"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  useSocket,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  useSocketListener,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ServerToClientPayload,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} from "wasp/client/webSocket"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const ChatPage = () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const [messageText, setMessageText] = useState<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // We are using a helper type to get the payload type for the "chatMessage" event.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    ClientToServerPayload<"chatMessage">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  >("")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const [messages, setMessages] = useState<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    ServerToClientPayload<"chatMessage">[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  >([])\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // The "socket" instance is typed with the types you defined on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const { socket, isConnected } = useSocket()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // This is a type-safe event handler: "chatMessage" event and its payload type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // are defined on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  useSocketListener("chatMessage", logMessage)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  function logMessage(msg: ServerToClientPayload<"chatMessage">) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    setMessages((priorMessages) => [msg, ...priorMessages])\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    e.preventDefault()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // This is a type-safe event emitter: "chatMessage" event and its payload type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // are defined on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    socket.emit("chatMessage", messageText)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    setMessageText("")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const messageList = messages.map((msg) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <li key={msg.id}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <em>{msg.username}</em>: {msg.text}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </li>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ))\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const connectionIcon = isConnected ? "🟢" : "🔴"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <h2>Chat {connectionIcon}</h2>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              <input\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                type="text"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                value={messageText}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                onChange={(e) => setMessageText(e.target.value)}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              <button type="submit">Submit</button>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </form>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <ul>{messageList}</ul>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## API Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[API reference](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/WebSocket)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [WebSocket »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/WebSocket)\n'[39m +

                      [32m''[39m
                  }
                ]
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }
            },
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'L1rxUJWaFAQNad8b'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,
              output: {

                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'Title: \n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'URL Source: https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass.md\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Overview\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp supports username & password authentication out of the box with login and signup flows. It provides you with the server-side implementation and the UI components for the client side.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Setting Up Username & Password Authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To set up username authentication we need to:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Enable username authentication in the Wasp file\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Add the `User` entity\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Add the auth routes and pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Use Auth UI components in our pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Structure of the `main.wasp.ts` file we will end up with:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { SignupPage } from "./src/pages/auth" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Configuring e-mail authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  name: "myApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  wasp: { version: "^0.24" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  title: "My App",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`  head: ["<link rel='icon' href='/favicon.ico' />"],\n`[39m +
                      [32m'  auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // Defining routes and pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("SignupRoute", "/signup", page(SignupPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1. Enable Username Authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's start with adding the following to our `main.wasp.ts` file:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  name: "myApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  wasp: { version: "^0.24" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  title: "My App",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`  head: ["<link rel='icon' href='/favicon.ico' />"],\n`[39m +
                      [32m'  auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"    // 1. Specify the user entity (we'll define it next)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'    userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    methods: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      // 2. Enable username authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      usernameAndPassword: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about the `usernameAndPassword` auth method options in the [`UsernameAndPasswordConfig` API Reference](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/UsernameAndPasswordConfig).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2. Add the User Entity\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `User` entity can be as simple as including only the `id` field:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 3. Define the user entity\n'[39m +
                      [32m'model User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id Int @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Add your own fields below\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can read more about how the `User` is connected to the rest of the auth system and how you can access the user data in the [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities) section of the docs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 3. Add the Routes and Pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next, we need to define the routes and pages for the authentication pages.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Add the following to the `main.wasp.ts` file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { LoginPage, SignupPage } from "./src/pages/auth" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("LoginRoute", "/login", page(LoginPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("SignupRoute", "/signup", page(SignupPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll define the React components for these pages in the `src/pages/auth.tsx` file below.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 4. Create the Client Pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We are using [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) to style the pages. Read more about how to add it [here](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/guides/libraries/tailwind).\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's create a `auth.tsx` file in the `src/pages` folder and add the following to it:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/pages/auth.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { LoginForm, SignupForm } from "wasp/client/auth"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { Link } from "react-router"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export function LoginPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <Layout>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <LoginForm />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <br />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <span className="text-sm font-medium text-gray-900">\n'[39m +
                      [32m`        Don't have an account yet? <Link to="/signup">go to signup</Link>.\n`[39m +
                      [32m'      </span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </Layout>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export function SignupPage() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <Layout>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <SignupForm />\n'[39m +

                      [32m'      <span className="text-sm font-medium text-gray-900">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        I already have an account (<Link to="/login">go to login</Link>).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      </span>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </Layout>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// A layout component to center the content\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <div className="h-full w-full bg-white">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <div className="flex min-h-[75vh] min-w-full items-center justify-center">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <div className="h-full w-full max-w-sm bg-white p-5">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          <div>{children}</div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We imported the generated Auth UI components and used them in our pages. Read more about the Auth UI components [here](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/ui).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Conclusion\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"That's it! We have set up username authentication in our app. 🎉\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `wasp db migrate-dev` and then `wasp start` should give you a working app with username authentication. If you want to put some of the pages behind authentication, read the [auth overview docs](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::caution[Using multiple auth identities for a single user]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp currently doesn't support multiple auth identities for a single user. This means, for example, that a user can't have both an email-based auth identity and a Google-based auth identity. This is something we will add in the future with the introduction of the [account merging feature](https://github.com/wasp-lang/wasp/issues/954).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Account merging means that multiple auth identities can be merged into a single user account. For example, a user's email and Google identity can be merged into a single user account. Then the user can log in with either their email or Google account and they will be logged into the same account.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Protecting a page with `authRequired`[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#protecting-a-page-with-authrequired "Direct link to protecting-a-page-with-authrequired")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When declaring a page, you can set the `authRequired` property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you set it to `true`, only authenticated users can access the page. Unauthenticated users are redirected to a route defined by the `auth.onAuthFailedRedirectTo` field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"import Main from "./src/pages/Main" with { type: "ref" }export default app({  // ...  spec: [    route("MainRoute", "/", page(Main, { authRequired: true })),  ],})`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Requires auth method\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If `authRequired` is set to `true`, the page's React component (passed as the first argument to `page(...)`) receives the `user` object as a prop. Read more about the `user` object in the [Accessing the logged-in user section](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#accessing-the-logged-in-user).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Logout action[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#logout-action "Direct link to Logout action")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We provide an action for logging out the user. Here's how you can use it:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Accessing the logged-in user[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#accessing-the-logged-in-user "Direct link to Accessing the logged-in user")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can get access to the `user` object both on the server and on the client. The `user` object contains the logged-in user's data.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `user` object has all the fields that you defined in your `User` entity. In addition to that, it will also contain all the auth-related fields that Wasp stores. This includes things like the `username` or the email verification status. For example, if you have a user that signed up using an email and password, the `user` object might look like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`const user = {  // User data  id: "cluqsex9500017cn7i2hwsg17",  address: "Some address",  // Auth methods specific data  identities: {    email: {      id: "user@app.com",      isEmailVerified: true,      emailVerificationSentAt: "2024-04-08T10:06:02.204Z",      passwordResetSentAt: null,    },  },}`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can read more about how the `User` is connected to the rest of the auth system and how you can access the user data in the [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities) section of the docs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### On the client[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#on-the-client "Direct link to On the client")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are two ways to access the `user` object on the client:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   the `user` prop\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   the `useAuth` hook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Getting the `user` in authenticated routes[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#getting-the-user-in-authenticated-routes "Direct link to getting-the-user-in-authenticated-routes")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If the page's spec sets `authRequired` to `true`, the page's React component receives the `user` object as a prop. This is the simplest way to access the user inside an authenticated page:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"import Account from "./src/pages/Account" with { type: "ref" }export default app({  // ...  spec: [    route("AccountRoute", "/account", page(Account, {      authRequired: true    })),  ],})`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   JavaScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   TypeScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'src/pages/Account.jsx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`import Button from "./Button";import { logout } from "wasp/client/auth";const AccountPage = ({ user }) => {  return (    <div>      <Button onClick={logout}>Logout</Button>      {JSON.stringify(user, null, 2)}    </div>  );};export default AccountPage;`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Getting the `user` in non-authenticated routes[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/overview#getting-the-user-in-non-authenticated-routes "Direct link to getting-the-user-in-non-authenticated-routes")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp provides a React hook you can use in the client components - `useAuth`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This hook is a thin wrapper over Wasp's `useQuery` hook and returns data in the same format.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   JavaScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*   TypeScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'src/pages/MainPage.jsx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

              toolCallId: [32m'1lM7uYMEnvXjdowx'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webFetch'[39m,

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Web Sockets\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp provides a fully integrated WebSocket experience by utilizing [Socket.IO](https://socket.io/) on the client and server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We handle making sure your URLs are correctly setup, CORS is enabled, and provide a useful `useSocket` and `useSocketListener` abstractions for use in React components.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To get started, you need to:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Define your WebSocket logic on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Enable WebSockets in your Wasp file, and connect it with your server logic.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Use WebSockets on the client, in React, via `useSocket` and `useSocketListener`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Optionally, type the WebSocket events and payloads for full-stack type safety.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's go through setting up WebSockets step by step, starting with enabling WebSockets in your Wasp file.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Turn On WebSockets in Your Wasp File\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We specify that we are using WebSockets by adding `webSocket` to our `app` and providing the required `fn`. You can optionally change the auto-connect behavior.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { webSocketFn } from "./src/webSocket" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  name: "myApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  webSocket: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    fn: webSocketFn,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    autoConnect: true, // optional, default: true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Defining the Events Handler\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's define the WebSockets server with all of the events and handler functions.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Full-stack type safety]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Check this out: we'll define the event types and payloads on the server, and they will be **automatically exposed on the client**. This helps you avoid mistakes when emitting events or handling them.\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### `webSocketFn` Function {#websocketfn}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'On the server, you will get Socket.IO `io: Server` argument and `context` for your WebSocket function. The `context` object give you access to all of the entities from your Wasp app.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use this `io` object to register callbacks for all the regular [Socket.IO events](https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-api/). Also, if a user is logged in, you will have a `socket.data.user` on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is how we can define our `webSocketFn` function:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/webSocket.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { v4 as uuidv4 } from "uuid"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type WebSocketDefinition, type WaspSocketData } from "wasp/server/webSocket"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const webSocketFn: WebSocketFn = (io, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  io.on("connection", (socket) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    const username = socket.data.user?.getFirstProviderUserId() ?? "Unknown"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    console.log("a user connected: ", username)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    socket.on("chatMessage", async (msg) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      console.log("message: ", msg)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      io.emit("chatMessage", { id: uuidv4(), username, text: msg })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      // You can also use your entities here:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      // await context.entities.SomeEntity.create({ someField: msg })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Typing our WebSocket function with the events and payloads\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// allows us to get type safety on the client as well\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type WebSocketFn = WebSocketDefinition<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ClientToServerEvents,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ServerToClientEvents,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  InterServerEvents,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  SocketData\n'[39m +
                      [32m'>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface ServerToClientEvents {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  chatMessage: (msg: { id: string, username: string, text: string }) => void;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface ClientToServerEvents {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  chatMessage: (msg: string) => void;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface InterServerEvents {}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Data that is attached to the socket.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// NOTE: Wasp automatically injects the JWT into the connection,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// and if present/valid, the server adds a user to the socket.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface SocketData extends WaspSocketData {}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Using the WebSocket On The Client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Full-stack type safety]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All the hooks we use are typed with the events and payloads you defined on the server. VS Code will give you autocomplete for the events and payloads, and you will get type errors if you make a mistake.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### The `useSocket` Hook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Client access to WebSockets is provided by the `useSocket` hook. It returns:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `socket: Socket` for sending and receiving events.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `isConnected: boolean` for showing a display of the Socket.IO connection status.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  - Note: Wasp automatically connects and establishes a WebSocket connection from the client to the server by default, so you do not need to explicitly `socket.connect()` or `socket.disconnect()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  - If you set `autoConnect: false` in your Wasp file, then you should call these as needed.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All components using `useSocket` share the same underlying `socket`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### The `useSocketListener` Hook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Additionally, there is a `useSocketListener: (event, callback) => void` hook which is used for registering event handlers. It takes care of unregistering the handler on unmount.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp's **full-stack type safety** kicks in here: all the event types and payloads are automatically inferred from the server and are available on the client.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can additionally use the `ClientToServerPayload` and `ServerToClientPayload` helper types to get the payload type for a specific event.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```tsx title="src/ChatPage.tsx"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import React, { useState } from "react"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  useSocket,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  useSocketListener,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ServerToClientPayload,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} from "wasp/client/webSocket"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const ChatPage = () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const [messageText, setMessageText] = useState<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // We are using a helper type to get the payload type for the "chatMessage" event.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    ClientToServerPayload<"chatMessage">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  >("")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const [messages, setMessages] = useState<\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    ServerToClientPayload<"chatMessage">[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  >([])\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // The "socket" instance is typed with the types you defined on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const { socket, isConnected } = useSocket()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // This is a type-safe event handler: "chatMessage" event and its payload type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // are defined on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  useSocketListener("chatMessage", logMessage)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  function logMessage(msg: ServerToClientPayload<"chatMessage">) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    setMessages((priorMessages) => [msg, ...priorMessages])\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    e.preventDefault()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // This is a type-safe event emitter: "chatMessage" event and its payload type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // are defined on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    socket.emit("chatMessage", messageText)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    setMessageText("")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const messageList = messages.map((msg) => (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <li key={msg.id}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <em>{msg.username}</em>: {msg.text}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </li>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ))\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const connectionIcon = isConnected ? "🟢" : "🔴"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    <>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <h2>Chat {connectionIcon}</h2>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              <input\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                type="text"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                value={messageText}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'                onChange={(e) => setMessageText(e.target.value)}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              />\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            <div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'              <button type="submit">Submit</button>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'            </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'          </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        </form>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'        <ul>{messageList}</ul>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      </div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    </>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## API Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[API reference](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/WebSocket)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### [WebSocket »](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/WebSocket)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[All the options for the webSocket field of the app spec.](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/WebSocket)\n'[39m +
                      [32m''[39m
                  }
                ]
              },
              providerOptions: {
                vertex: {
                  thoughtSignature: [32m''[39m
                }
              }

              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'L1rxUJWaFAQNad8b'[39m,

              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'Title: \n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'URL Source: https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/username-and-pass.md\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Markdown Content:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://wasp.sh/llms.txt\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Overview\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp supports username & password authentication out of the box with login and signup flows. It provides you with the server-side implementation and the UI components for the client side.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Setting Up Username & Password Authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To set up username authentication we need to:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'  name: "myApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  wasp: { version: "^0.24" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  title: "My App",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`  head: ["<link rel='icon' href='/favicon.ico' />"],\n`[39m +

                      [32m'    // Defining routes and pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    route("SignupRoute", "/signup", page(SignupPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1. Enable Username Authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's start with adding the following to our `main.wasp.ts` file:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  name: "myApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  wasp: { version: "^0.24" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  title: "My App",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`  head: ["<link rel='icon' href='/favicon.ico' />"],\n`[39m +
                      [32m'  auth: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"    // 1. Specify the user entity (we'll define it next)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'    userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    methods: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      // 2. Enable username authentication\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      usernameAndPassword: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about the `usernameAndPassword` auth method options in the [`UsernameAndPasswordConfig` API Reference](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/UsernameAndPasswordConfig).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2. Add the User Entity\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `User` entity can be as simple as including only the `id` field:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 3. Define the user entity\n'[39m +
                      [32m'model User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id Int @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // Add your own fields below\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can read more about how the `User` is connected to the rest of the auth system and how you can access the user data in the [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities) section of the docs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 3. Add the Routes and Pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next, we need to define the routes and pages for the authentication pages.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { LoginPage, SignupPage } from "./src/pages/auth" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +

                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll define the React components for these pages in the `src/pages/auth.tsx` file below.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Including the User with Other Entities[​](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/auth/entities#including-the-user-with-other-entities "Direct link to Including the User with Other Entities")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Sometimes, you might want to include the user's data when fetching other entities. For example, you might want to include the user's data with the tasks they have created.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you have some **piece of the auth data that you want to access frequently** (for example the `username`), it's best to store it at the top level of the `User` entity.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For example, save the `username` or `email` as a property on the `User` and you'll be able to access it without including the `auth` and `identities` fields.                       [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'## Working with Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You declare queries in the Wasp file and implement them using NodeJS. Wasp not only runs these queries within the server's context but also creates code that enables you to call them from any part of your codebase, whether it's on the client or server side.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This means you don't have to build an HTTP API for your query, manage server-side request handling, or even deal with client-side response handling and caching.                       [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a Query, you must:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Declare the Query in Wasp using the `query` spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. Define the Query's NodeJS implementation.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"After completing these two steps, you'll be able to use the Query from any point in your code.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Specifying Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a Query in Wasp, we begin with a `query` spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's declare two Queries - one to fetch all tasks, and another to fetch tasks based on a filter, such as whether a task is done:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, query } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getAllTasks, getFilteredTasks } from "./src/queries" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    query(getAllTasks),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    query(getFilteredTasks),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to know about all supported options for the `query` spec, take a look at the [API Reference](#api-reference).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::note\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When `main.wasp.ts` needs to point to your code, it uses imports like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Notice the `with { type: "ref" }` part at the end of the import statement. For more details and examples, see [reference imports](https://wasp.sh/docs/general/spec#reference-imports).\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You might have noticed that we told Wasp to import Query implementations that don't yet exist. Don't worry about that for now. We'll write the implementations imported from `queries.ts` in the next section.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's a good idea to start with the high-level concept (the Query spec in the Wasp file) and only then deal with the implementation details (the Query's implementation in JavaScript).\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"After declaring a Wasp Query, Wasp derives the Query's name from the function you pass to `query`. For example, `query(getFilteredTasks)` creates a Query named `getFilteredTasks`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Two important things then happen:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

This function takes a single optional argument - an object containing any serializable data you wish to use inside the Query. Wasp will send this object over the network and pass it into the Query's implementation as its first positional argument (more on this when we look at the implementations). Such an abstraction works thanks to an HTTP API route handler Wasp generates on the server, which calls the Query's NodeJS implementation under the hood.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Generating these two functions ensures a similar calling interface across the entire app (both client and server).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Implementing Queries in Node\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Now that we've declared the Query, what remains is to implement it. We've instructed Wasp to look for the Queries' implementations in the file `src/queries.ts`, so that's where we should export them from.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's how you might implement the previously declared Queries `getAllTasks` and `getFilteredTasks`:\n"[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Task = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: number\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  description: string\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  isDone: boolean\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// our "database"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const tasks: Task[] = [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { id: 1, description: "Buy some eggs", isDone: true },\n'[39m +

                      [32m'  { id: 3, description: "Eat breakfast", isDone: false },\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// You don't need to use the arguments if you don't need them\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export const getAllTasks: GetAllTasks<void, Task[]> = () => {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// The 'args' object is something sent by the caller (most often from the client)\n"[39m +

                      [32m'> = (args) => {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp will automatically handle the serialization and deserialization [for all the data types that superjson supports](https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/superjson#decimaljs--prismadecimal:~\\:text=Superjson%20supports%20many%20extra%20types) (like `biging`, `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, etc.), and for [Prisma.Decimal](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/special-fields-and-types#working-with-decimal).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Type support for Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp automatically generates the types `GetAllTasks` and `GetFilteredTasks` based on your Wasp file's specs:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `GetAllTasks` is a generic type automatically generated by Wasp, based on the Query spec for `getAllTasks`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `GetFilteredTasks` is also a generic type automatically generated by Wasp, based on the Query spec for `getFilteredTasks`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Use these types to type the Query's implementation. It's optional but very helpful since doing so properly types the Query's context.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, TypeScript will know the `context.entities` object must include the `Task` entity. TypeScript also knows whether the `context` object includes user information (it depends on whether your Query uses auth).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The generated types are generic and accept two optional type arguments: `Input` and `Output`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. `Input` - The argument (the payload) received by the Query function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. `Output` - The Query function's return type.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Use these type arguments to type the Query's inputs and outputs.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Explanation for the example above\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The above code says that the Query `getAllTasks` doesn't expect any arguments (its input type is `void`), but it does return a list of tasks (its output type is `Task[]`).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'On the other hand, the Query `getFilteredTasks` expects an object of type `{ isDone: boolean }`. This type is derived from the `Task` entity type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you don't care about typing the Query's inputs and outputs, you can omit both type arguments. TypeScript will then infer the most general types (`never` for the input and `unknown` for the output).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Specifying `Input` or `Output` is completely optional, but we highly recommended it. Doing so gives you:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Type support for the arguments and the return value inside the implementation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Full-stack type safety**. We'll explore what this means when we discuss calling the Query from the client.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about type support for implementing Queries in the [API Reference](#implementing-queries).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::tip[Inferring the return type]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If don't want to explicitly type the Query's return value, the `satisfies` keyword tells TypeScript to infer it automatically:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const getFoo = (async (_args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const foos = await context.entities.Foo.findMany()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    foos,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    message: "Here are some foos!",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    queriedAt: new Date(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}) satisfies GetFoo\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'From the snippet above, TypeScript knows:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. The correct type for `context`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. The Query's return type is `{ foos: Foo[], message: string, queriedAt: Date }`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you don't need the context, you can skip specifying the Query's type (and arguments):\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const getFoo = () => ({ name: "Foo", date: new Date() })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m"Actions are declared in Wasp and implemented in NodeJS. Wasp runs Actions within the server's context, but it also generates code that allows you to call them from anywhere in your code (either client or server) using the same interface.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This means you don't have to worry about building an HTTP API for the Action, managing server-side request handling, or even dealing with client-side response handling and caching. Instead, just focus on developing the business logic inside your Action, and let Wasp handle the rest!\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create an Action, you need to:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Declare the Action in Wasp using the `action` spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. Implement the Action's NodeJS functionality.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once these two steps are completed, you can use the Action from anywhere in your code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Specifying Actions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To create an Action in Wasp, we begin with an `action` spec. Let's declare two Actions - one for creating a task, and another for marking tasks as done:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { action, app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createTask, markTaskAsDone } from "./src/actions" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  // ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    action(createTask),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    action(markTaskAsDone),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to know about all supported options for the `action` spec, take a look at the [API Reference](#api-reference).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::note\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When `main.wasp.ts` needs to point to your code, it uses imports like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Notice the `with { type: "ref" }` part at the end of the import statement. This tells Wasp to treat the import as a reference to your app\'s code, without running the imported code. For more details and examples, see [reference imports](https://wasp.sh/docs/general/spec#reference-imports).\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You might have noticed that we told Wasp to import Action implementations that don't yet exist. Don't worry about that for now. We'll write the implementations imported from `actions.ts` in the next section.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's a good idea to start with the high-level concept (the Action spec in the Wasp file) and only then deal with the implementation details (the Action's implementation in JavaScript).\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"After declaring a Wasp Action, Wasp derives the Action's name from the function you pass to `action`. For example, `action(markTaskAsDone)` creates an Action named `markTaskAsDone`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Two important things then happen:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Wasp **generates a server-side NodeJS function** with the Action's name.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Wasp **generates a client-side JavaScript function** with the Action's name (e.g., `markTaskAsDone`). This function takes a single optional argument - an object containing any serializable data you wish to use inside the Action. Wasp will send this object over the network and pass it into the Action's implementation as its first positional argument (more on this when we look at the implementations). Such an abstraction works thanks to an HTTP API route handler Wasp generates on the server, which calls the Action's NodeJS implementation under the hood.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Generating these two functions ensures a similar calling interface across the entire app (both client and server).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Implementing Actions in Node\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Now that we've declared the Action, what remains is to implement it. We've instructed Wasp to look for the Actions' implementations in the file `src/actions.ts`, so that's where we should export them from.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's how you might implement the previously declared Actions `createTask` and `markTaskAsDone`:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="src/actions.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type CreateTask, type MarkTaskAsDone } from "wasp/server/operations"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Task = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  id: number\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  description: string\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  isDone: boolean\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// our "database"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'let nextId = 4\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const tasks = [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { id: 1, description: "Buy some eggs", isDone: true },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { id: 2, description: "Make an omelette", isDone: false },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  { id: 3, description: "Eat breakfast", isDone: false },\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// You don't need to use the arguments if you don't need them\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export const createTask: CreateTask<Pick<Task, "description">, Task> = (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  args\n'[39m +
                      [32m') => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const newTask = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    id: nextId,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    isDone: false,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    description: args.description,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  nextId += 1\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  tasks.push(newTask)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return newTask\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// The 'args' object is something sent by the caller (most often from the client)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export const markTaskAsDone: MarkTaskAsDone<Pick<Task, "id">, void> = (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  args\n'[39m +
                      [32m') => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const task = tasks.find((task) => task.id === args.id)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  if (!task) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"    // We'll show how to properly handle such errors later\n"[39m +
                      [32m'    return\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  task.isDone = true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::info[Payload constraints]\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp uses [superjson](https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/superjson) under the hood. This means you're not limited to only sending and receiving JSON payloads.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp will automatically handle the serialization and deserialization [for all the data types that superjson supports](https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/superjson#decimaljs--prismadecimal:~\\:text=Superjson%20supports%20many%20extra%20types) (like `biging`, `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, etc.), and for [Prisma.Decimal](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/special-fields-and-types#working-with-decimal).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"As long as you're annotating your Operations with the correct automatically generated types, TypeScript ensures your payloads are valid (i.e., Wasp knows how to serialize and deserialize them).\n"[39m +
                      [32m':::\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Type support for Actions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp automatically generates the types `CreateTask` and `MarkTaskAsDone` based on the specs in your Wasp file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `CreateTask` is a generic type that Wasp automatically generated based on the Action spec for `createTask`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `MarkTaskAsDone` is a generic type that Wasp automatically generated based on the Action spec for `markTaskAsDone`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Use these types to type the Action's implementation. It's optional but very helpful since doing so properly types the Action's context.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, TypeScript will know the `context.entities` object must include the `Task` entity. TypeScript also knows whether the `context` object includes user information (it depends on whether your Action uses auth).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The generated types are generic and accept two optional type arguments: `Input` and `Output`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. `Input` - The argument (the payload) received by the Action function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. `Output` - The Action function's return type.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Use these type arguments to type the Action's inputs and outputs.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Explanation for the example above\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The above code says that the Action `createTask` expects an object with the new task's description (its input type is `Pick<Task, 'description'>`) and returns the new task (its output type is `Task`).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"On the other hand, the Action `markTaskAsDone` expects an object of type `Pick<Task, 'id'>`. This type is derived from the `Task` entity type.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you don't care about typing the Action's inputs and outputs, you can omit both type arguments. TypeScript will then infer the most general types (`never` for the input and `unknown` for the output).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Specifying `Input` or `Output` is completely optional, but we highly recommended it. Doing so gives you:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Type support for the arguments and the return value inside the implementation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Full-stack type safety**. We'll explore what this means when we discuss calling the Action from the client.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read more about type support for implementing Actions in the [API Reference](#implementing-actions).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::tip[Inferring the return type]\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const createFoo = (async (_args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  const foo = await context.entities.Foo.create()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  return {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    newFoo: foo,\n'[39m +
                      [32m`    message: "Here's your foo!",\n`[39m +
                      [32m'    returnedAt: new Date(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}) satisfies CreateFoo\n'[39m +
